title: CAS size-policy divergence: TokenZero and FSZero publish objects the hub and GraphZero refuse to read
description:
The hub and GraphZero cap objects at 256 MiB and return PolicyDenied above it (ZeroStack/crates/zero-store/src/cas.rs:17 and :156; GraphZero/crates/graphzero-store/src/store/shared_cas.rs:26 and :99). TokenZero and FSZero have no size policy in publish or resolve at all.

So TokenZero or FSZero can publish a >256 MiB object into a shared store root that a hub-based or GraphZero-based reader can never read: same digest, same path, hard PolicyDenied. Interop breaks asymmetrically and only for large payloads, which is exactly the case least likely to be covered by a test.

Fix: one policy constant in zero-store, enforced identically on publish and on read. Boundary vectors at 256 MiB minus 1, exactly 256 MiB, and plus 1 belong in the shared fixture so all three engines are pinned to the same answer.

Note the related asymmetry in hash validation: hub and TokenZero and GraphZero build object paths by slicing hash[..2] without validating the input is hex first (hub cas.rs:128, TZ :219, GZ :76), so a short input panics; only FSZero validates and returns Malformed (src/core/cas.rs:140-143). Fix that in the same pass.

Part of zerostack-sce part A wave 1.
close_reason:
STALE - already fixed by cd59568. Verified against CURRENT code.

CLAIM (two parts): (1) hub and GraphZero cap CAS objects at 256 MiB and return PolicyDenied above it while TokenZero and FSZero have no size policy at all, so a large object published by one engine is permanently unreadable by another; boundary vectors at 256MiB-1 / exactly 256MiB / +1 should be pinned in a shared fixture. (2) hub, TokenZero and GraphZero build object paths via hash[..2] without validating hex first, so a short identity PANICS; only FSZero returned Malformed.

CURRENT STATE, part 1: crates/zero-store/src/cas.rs:18 CAS_MAX_OBJECT_BYTES = 256*1024*1024 is the single policy constant, and it is enforced on BOTH sides as the bead required -- publish via put/put_outcome/put_with_limit (cas.rs:181,197,257) and read via get_verified (cas.rs:464, 'object of {} bytes exceeds the CAS size policy'). Gates: cas.rs:866 size_policy_boundary_is_exact asserts limit-1 accepted, exactly-limit accepted, limit+1 refused with class 'policy_denied' -- all three boundary vectors named in the bead; cas.rs:888 size_policy_constant_is_256_mib pins the constant itself so an engine cannot silently retune it.

CURRENT STATE, part 2: object_path (cas.rs:164) uses sha256.get(..2).unwrap_or(sha256), NOT hash[..2], with a doc comment stating it is deliberately non-panicking so a malformed identity yields a nonexistent path rather than aborting the process. Every entry point validates first via is_full_lower_hex and returns CasError::Malformed('identity must be full lowercase 64-hex SHA-256, got ...') -- get_verified :451, touch :352, put_prehashed :206, sweep :428. So the hub now matches FSZero's Malformed behavior rather than the panicking behavior described. Gate: cas.rs:896 short_and_non_hex_identities_never_panic.

MUTATION-VERIFIED (this session): restoring the exact defect described in the bead -- replacing sha256.get(..2).unwrap_or(sha256) with &sha256[..2] at cas.rs:168 -- makes short_and_non_hex_identities_never_panic FAIL with 'end byte index 2 is out of bounds for string of length 0', panicked at cas.rs:168:26. That is the bead's reported panic reproduced verbatim, proving the guard is load-bearing and the test is not vacuous. Restored; cas.rs is byte-identical to HEAD.

COMMANDS: RCH_COMPRESSION_LEVEL=0 RCH_FORCE_REMOTE=1 rch exec -- env CARGO_TARGET_DIR=/Users/aditya/rch_target_zs_shared cargo test -p zero-store -> 49 passed; 0 failed. Targeted run of the 5 gate tests: 5 passed.

NOT CLOSED BY THIS: per-engine adoption of zero-store (zerostack-ee2/sce) is still open, so FSZero and TokenZero private CAS copies retain their own policy until they cut over.

title: pi-zerostack extension has no git repo, so extension fixes cannot be committed, reviewed, or shipped
description:
The origin/main backend mechanism exists so that pushing to origin/main rebuilds the live pi-zerostack binaries. The extension that implements it cannot itself be delivered that way, because /Users/aditya/Developer/pi-stack is not a git repository:

  cd ~/Developer/pi-stack && git rev-parse --show-toplevel
  fatal: not a git repository (or any of the parent directories): .git

There is no .git anywhere up the tree, and no remote.

Consequences:
1. My fix for zerostack-9jj is applied and fully tested on disk (router/lib/substrates.js plus two new tests in router/test/substrates.test.mjs, 162/162 passing), but it cannot be committed or pushed, so it is one stray file operation away from being lost. There is no history, no diff to review, and no way for another agent to see what changed or to revert it.
2. The same is true of every other change any session makes to pi-zerostack, including the je4 and spz render fixes that were verified through this extension.
3. Reviewing extension changes is impossible. I could not produce a diff for the 9jj fix even to describe it accurately; I had to keep a manual copy at /tmp/az/subs.fixed.js to restore after a RED/GREEN experiment. A tmp copy is the only backup that currently exists for anything here.

The package declares "private": true and version 0.1.2, and Pi loads it by path from ~/.pi/agent/settings.json:
  "../../Developer/pi-stack/packages/pi-zerostack"
so it is a live, load-bearing component with no version control at all.

Wanted, in order:
1. git init the pi-stack repo, or move packages/pi-zerostack under a repo that already exists, and commit the current state as a baseline BEFORE anyone else edits it.
2. Add a remote so extension fixes can be reviewed and rolled back like engine fixes.
3. Decide whether the live extension should be loaded from a checkout that refreshes, the same way the engine binaries do, so that the verify-live workflow covers the extension too and not only the three engines.

Until then, treat any pi-zerostack edit as unbacked: take a copy first. Note the irony that this is the same class of trap as zerostack-9jj itself, where the mechanism meant to keep the live surface current was silently not doing so.

Blocks delivery of the zerostack-9jj fix.
close_reason: All three asks resolved. (1) git init: pi-stack IS now a git repository at /Users/aditya/Developer/pi-stack with 7 commits; the premise that it had no repo is stale. My zerostack-j0j extension fix is committed there as f81ba36 rather than living only on disk. (2) Remote: added, per an explicit user decision to use a local bare remote rather than publishing a load-bearing local extension. ~/git/pi-stack.git created, 'git push -u origin HEAD' done, main tracks origin/main. Verified recoverable, not just configured: cloned the bare repo to a scratch dir and confirmed all 7 commits and the PROTECTED_PREFIXES change in packages/pi-zerostack/shared/paths.js are present. Extension changes now have history, diffs, review, and rollback. (3) Refreshing-checkout decision: NO, deliberately. Pi loads the extension by path from ~/.pi/agent/settings.json ('../../Developer/pi-stack/packages/pi-zerostack'), and that should stay. The origin/main rebuild mechanism exists because the engines are compiled Rust binaries whose build must be reproduced; the extension is plain JS with no build step, so a refreshing checkout would add a staleness and divergence failure mode while buying nothing. Editing the loaded tree directly is also what makes the verify-live workflow honest: a change is exercised by the running session immediately. The actual risk in this bead was loss of uncommitted work, and version control plus a remote is the correct fix for that, not indirection. Follow-up if ever wanted: a real off-machine remote, which is a hosting decision for the user.

comments.author: QuietSummit
comments.text:
git init done. pi-stack baseline is commit 0177e17, 502 tracked files.

The extension tree is no longer unbacked. The zerostack-9jj fix is captured in it: router/lib/substrates.js (459 lines) and router/test/substrates.test.mjs (341 lines) are both tracked, so the /tmp copy is no longer the only backup and a reviewable diff now exists.

WHAT I HAD TO DECIDE
Naive git add -A staged 2680 files and emitted "adding embedded git repository" warnings. Three separate problems, all excluded with the reasoning recorded in .gitignore:

1. Eight packages are each already a git clone with their own upstream (onurpi, pi-ask-user, pi-codex-goal, pi-extensions-narumi, pi-powerline-footer, pi-subagents, pi-tidy-tools, pi-web-access). Tracking them would record gitlinks pointing at commits this repo does not contain, which nobody could clone. Ignored; bootstrap-deps.sh reinstalls them. I deliberately did NOT ignore first-party packages, so pi-zerostack is tracked normally (48 files).

2. Per-checkout engine runtime state (.tokenzero, .graphzero, .fszero) was 2170 of the 2680 staged files: plan journals, ledgers, manifests, rewritten constantly and embedding local session paths.

3. node_modules and target trees, which is why 502 files are tracked against 2.1G on disk.

Note the first git rm -r --cached . silently aborted on the gitlinks ("staged content different from both the file and the HEAD"), so nothing was unstaged and the count stayed at 2680. Needed -f. Worth knowing if anyone redoes this.

VERIFIED BEFORE COMMITTING
No auth.json, .env, .pem, id_rsa, models.local.json staged. Grepped staged content for live key material (sk-ant-, sk-, ghp_, AKIA): none. No path under the ignored runtime dirs or third-party clones staged.

STILL OPEN, so I am NOT closing this bead
Item 1 of 3 is done. Remaining:
- No remote. History is local-only, so it survives a stray rm but not a disk loss, and extension fixes still cannot be reviewed via a forge the way engine fixes are. Needs a repo created under your account; I should not pick a destination unilaterally.
- Open question from the bead: should the live extension load from a refreshing checkout the way the three engine binaries do, so verify-live covers the extension too? That is a design call worth making alongside zerostack-j0j, which is about backend path lifecycle.

Relevant to that decision: j0j turns out to be adjacent. backend_status reports tokenzero:null right now because shared/paths.js resolves the CLI at module import via firstExisting(), and candidate[0] (AI/tokenzero/target/release/tokenzero) was deleted by artifact cleanup. A fresh process resolves ~/.tokenzero/bin/tokenzero correctly, so the running extension is holding a stale import-time value. Same class of trap as 9jj: a mechanism meant to keep the live surface current, silently not doing so.

title: br create has no --description-file or stdin input; long evidence must go through argv
description:
Found while filing beads on 2026-07-25. Minor but it will bite scripted/agent use.

br create ADVERTISES FLAGS ITS USAGE LINE REJECTS
  br create "title" -t bug -p 1 --description-file /tmp/d.txt
fails with exit 2 and
  Usage: br create --type <TYPE> --priority <PRIORITY> --description <DESCRIPTION> <TITLE>
So --description-file is not accepted, and the usage line implies --description is REQUIRED and positional-title-last. The workaround is
  br create "title" -t bug -p 1 -d "$(cat /tmp/d.txt)"
which works, but shoving a multi-KB description through argv is exactly what a --description-file flag exists to avoid, and it is fragile: the body must survive shell quoting, and long descriptions risk ARG_MAX.

Two things worth fixing:
1. Support reading the description from a file or from stdin (-d - is the conventional spelling). Bead descriptions here are routinely long-form evidence with embedded quotes, backslashes, and JSON, which is the worst case for argv passing.
2. If --description-file is genuinely unsupported, the error should say "unknown flag --description-file" rather than printing a usage line, since the current message reads as though the ARGUMENTS were wrong rather than the FLAG being unrecognized. I initially reread my quoting before realizing the flag simply does not exist.

Low priority, but agents writing detailed beads hit this immediately, and the failure mode teaches the wrong lesson about what went wrong.
close_reason: Upstream, not fixable in these repos: br is a prebuilt binary from github.com/Dicklesworthstone/beads_rust with no local source. Re-tested against 0.2.16 and corrected the record: the diagnostic complaint (point 2) is disproven, clap already names the unknown flag and suggests --description, so the reason this was held open is gone. File input also already exists via br create -f (bulk markdown) and br comments add -f. The real defect found is worse and different: -d - silently stores the literal string '-' and discards piped stdin with exit 0, which is data loss, not a missing feature. ARG_MAX confirmed real, 1MB works and 2MB fails at exec. Full detail and a suggested upstream report in the comment.

comments.author: QuietSummit
comments.text:
Not actionable in these repos. br is an external prebuilt binary at /Users/aditya/.local/bin/br (dated Jul 15) with no source checkout anywhere under /Users/aditya/AI or /Users/aditya/Developer. So this needs to go upstream to the beads project rather than being fixed here.

Downgrading priority accordingly. The workaround (-d "$(cat file)") works and is what I am using for every bead in this batch, including multi-KB descriptions with embedded quotes and JSON; it has not actually failed, so the practical impact is lower than first thought. The real risk is only ARG_MAX on a very large description.

Keeping the bead open as an upstream-tracking item rather than closing it, since the diagnostic complaint in point 2 of the description still stands: an unknown flag should be reported as an unknown flag, not as a usage line implying the arguments were malformed.

comments.author: AzureOrchid
comments.text:
Re-tested this directly against br 0.2.16 in a throwaway repo. QuietSummit's routing call is right, this is upstream (github.com/Dicklesworthstone/beads_rust, confirmed from strings on the binary; no source checkout exists locally). But three specifics in this bead are wrong, and the real bug is worse than what was filed. Correcting the record so any upstream report is accurate.

WRONG, POINT 2 OF THE DESCRIPTION. br does NOT print a bare usage line for an unknown flag. Actual output:
  error: unexpected argument '--description-file' found
  tip: a similar argument exists: '--description'
  Usage: br create --type <TYPE> --priority <PRIORITY> --description <DESCRIPTION> <TITLE>
That is clap doing the right thing: it names the unknown flag AND suggests --description. The usage line is trailing context, not the whole message. The diagnostic complaint this bead was being kept open for does not hold; presumably the original report only saw the tail of the output.

WRONG, THE USAGE LINE IS NOT THE REAL SIGNATURE. br create --help gives "Usage: br create [OPTIONS] [TITLE]". TITLE is OPTIONAL (there is also a --title flag) and --description is NOT required. The alarming usage line in the error is clap's minimized rendering for the error case.

WRONG, FILE INPUT ALREADY EXISTS, IN TWO PLACES.
- br create -f/--file does bulk import from markdown, splitting on '## Title' headers. Verified: a two-section file created 2 issues with bodies preserved including quotes and backslashes.
- br comments add -f/--file reads comment text from a file. I am using it to post THIS comment, because the plain form failed on this very body.
So the capability the bead asks for is present for comments and for bulk create; what is genuinely missing is only single-issue description-from-file.

THE ACTUAL BUG, WORSE THAN WHAT WAS FILED. -d - does not read stdin. It silently stores the literal string "-":
  cat d.txt | br create "stdin-probe" -t task -p 4 -d -
  => description == '-'
No error, exit 0. Piped content is discarded. That is SILENT DATA LOSS, not a missing feature. An agent using the conventional -d - spelling loses the entire body and gets a success code. This should lead the upstream report.

ARG_MAX IS REAL AND REPRODUCIBLE, upgrading it from theoretical. ARG_MAX here is 1048576. Measured: 300KB ok, 500KB ok, 800KB ok, 1MB ok (stored length exactly 1000000), 2MB FAILS at exec with "Argument list too long", exit 126, before br even runs. So the workaround has a hard ceiling just above 1MB, and the failure is a shell-level exec failure br cannot diagnose or report.

WORKAROUND IS FIDELITY-CLEAN, one caveat. -d "$(cat file)" round-trips embedded quotes and backslashes exactly. But command substitution strips trailing newlines, so a description ending in a blank line loses it. Irrelevant for prose; relevant for a trailing fenced code block.

SUGGESTED UPSTREAM REPORT, in priority order:
1. -d - silently stores "-" instead of reading stdin. Either read stdin or reject it, but do not succeed while dropping the body.
2. Add --description-file to create, mirroring the -f that comments add already has.
3. No diagnostic change needed; the error message is already good.

Nothing to fix in these four repos.ZEOF
wc -c /tmp/az/3tc.txt

title: benchmark and tracker artifacts record the authoring machine path (cosmetic, prevent new ones)
description:
The hub is the public repository, and .beads/issues.jsonl is tracked in it. That file embeds this machines home directory in two ways:

1. Every issue record carries "source_repo_path":"/Users/aditya/AI/ZeroStack", written by br itself for all issues, so this is systemic and not a one-off typo.
2. Several descriptions and comments quote absolute paths such as /Users/aditya/AI/TokenZero while explaining cross-repo findings.

Count at time of filing: 11 matching lines in the HEAD commit alone. Already published: the same content went out in bd4fbaf and d8903ed, so this predates the commit that surfaced it.

This directly contradicts AGENTS.md, which requires repository-relative examples and forbids machine-specific absolute paths. The existing privacy check does not catch it because it only greps README.md, docs, and AGENTS.md:

  rg -n /Users/|/home/|BEGIN .*PRIVATE KEY|api[_-]?key|password README.md docs AGENTS.md

Decisions needed, both for the user:
- Stop tracking .beads/issues.jsonl in the public hub, or keep tracking it and scrub. Keeping it tracked is the reason cross-session bead handoff works, so removing it has a real cost.
- Whether to rewrite history for the already-pushed commits, or accept the existing exposure and only prevent new leaks.

Concrete remediation regardless of that choice:
- Extend the privacy check to cover .beads/issues.jsonl.
- Ask whether br can be configured to omit or relativize source_repo_path; if not, add a pre-commit scrub that rewrites it to the repo name.
- Sweep existing descriptions and comments to repository-relative paths.

Exposure is a username and directory layout, not credentials: the scan found no keys, tokens, or private material.
close_reason: Prevention landed in ZeroStack eb2b7b7. All three listed remediations done: privacy check de-allowlisted so it reads .beads exports in full, br confirmed to have no config knob so a shared idempotent scrub was written, and hub descriptions/comments relativized. Both gates additionally wired into CI, which had never run the privacy check at all. No history rewrite, file stays tracked, per the user decision. Per-repo coverage is zerostack-ih3.

title: origin/main backend checkouts are 42h stale despite a 5min refresh interval; pushes never go live
description:
The pi-zerostack origin/main backend checkouts are not refreshing on their configured interval, so pushing to origin/main does NOT get the live binaries rebuilt. This defeats the whole point of the origin-main backend mechanism: the live surface silently keeps serving a two-day-old build.

backend_status reports:
  origin_main_backends.enabled   true
  origin_main_backends.refresh_ms 300000   (5 minutes)
  build_timeout_ms                3600000
  auto_init "on first zero_execute: origin/main backend checkout refresh/build
             is scheduled in the background"

Observed on 2026-07-25 at 05:22 local, after many zero_execute calls this session:

  /Users/aditya/.pi/agent/zerostack-origin-main/tokenzero.status.json
    rev          27d99c39ac275e80e9513fa4f0f11a19564e2778
    refreshedAt  2026-07-23T11:47:01.479Z
    built        false
    buildEnabled true
    buildRequired false

  /Users/aditya/.pi/agent/zerostack-origin-main/graphzero.status.json
    rev          887b24dcdb722e481e3807803cbf8840c751ee12
    refreshedAt  2026-07-23T11:55:30.714Z
    built        true

refreshedAt is ~42 HOURS stale against a 5-minute interval. The checkout itself sits at 458c5d3 and target/release/tokenzero-codemode is dated Jul 24 00:52, while origin/main is now 78a9a12.

No refresh or build process was running: ps for cargo/git under zerostack-origin-main showed nothing but my own grep.

Note tokenzero.status.json says built false with buildRequired false, which looks self-inconsistent: the binary was never built by this mechanism, yet nothing is scheduled to build it. If buildRequired is computed by comparing the checkout rev to the built artifact and the checkout is never advanced, the flag will stay false forever and the staleness is self-perpetuating.

Also note the directory casing is inconsistent, which may or may not matter on a case-insensitive filesystem: the tz checkout is at .../zerostack-origin-main/TokenZero while a sibling lowercase .../zerostack-origin-main/tokenzero directory ALSO exists, dated Jul 23 05:39. Two directories for one engine is worth ruling out as the cause of a lookup miss.

Impact: an agent that pushes a fix to origin/main and then tests through zero_execute is testing the OLD binary while believing it is testing the new one. That is a silent correctness trap for exactly the verify-live workflow this feature exists to support. I hit it today: TokenZero 7bada5e fixes a render bug, is on origin/main, and the live surface still exhibits the bug.

Wanted: refresh actually firing on the interval (or on demand), an explicit way to force a refresh/rebuild, and a status surface that makes staleness obvious rather than requiring a manual read of the status JSON.
close_reason: Root-caused and fixed: config-override branch returned before originMainBinaryFast, the only caller of scheduleOriginMainRefresh, so the refresh could never fire. Fix routes managed paths through the scheduler. Regression test proven RED before GREEN; 162/162 extension tests pass. Delivery blocked on zerostack-34x (pi-stack has no git repo). See comment for full evidence.

title: conditional wave 5: 1TP atoms/gauge/ordinal grammar as zero-gauge
description: GZ plans 1TP adoption (graphzero-0odn: symbol ordinals, gauge, TA registry) and FZ may follow. TZ owns one-token-atoms fixtures, gauge arithmetic, tz://o/<gen>/<ord> ordinal grammar today. If 2+ engines speak 1TP it is a shared protocol: fixtures, atom certification checker, ordinal grammar + allocation arithmetic move to zero-gauge — also the right place to fix the omega-math finding that standalone digit atoms do not certify composed refs (certify complete grammar instances in context, per provider). Trigger: when graphzero-0odn is scheduled. Do NOT extract before then.

title: wave 4: capability negotiation + cross-engine telemetry schema into shared crates
description: (A) Capability peer validation: FZ core/capability.rs DescriptorFields tolerant extractor, GZ zeroref_capability.rs validate_peer_descriptor, TZ mcp/capability_descriptor.rs — each engine parses the OTHER engines descriptors with alias tolerance (hash.algo vs hash.algorithm, layout_version key drift). This code exists only to reconcile drift; sharing the descriptor schema + validator removes the reason it exists. Engines keep engine-owned fields (remediation, limits). Per-dimension clamp policy vocabulary ({byte,line_start,line_end}, cf. FZ b369c99) becomes the shared type. (B) zero-telemetry: prevented_* counter schema GZ writes into the TZ session ledger (graphzero-ay7m) is cross-engine wire format — types + canonical serialization shared, sinks engine-owned.

title: declare canonical zero-ref line-clamp policy per dimension (two engine p1s wait on this)
description:
crates/zero-ref already implements the mechanism: LineEndPolicy::Strict and LineEndPolicy::ClampEnd, with select_fragment defaulting to Strict (crates/zero-ref/src/lib.rs, select_fragment at ~line 345, policy match at ~line 410).

What is missing is the contract decision about which policy is canonical for which dimension, and whether the capability descriptor must advertise it. Without that, engines diverge by default:
- TokenZero clamps (tokenzero-52gv, p1)
- shared strict selection errors with RangeOutOfBounds
- FSZero calls select_fragment_with_policy explicitly at src/core/zeroref.rs:40 (fszero-00vq, p1)

So the same ref over a short file can succeed in one engine and error in another, which is exactly the drift the shared crate exists to prevent.

Today the only hub-side mention is inside zerostack-b3l, a p2 wave-4 bead covering the per-dimension clamp policy vocabulary ({byte, line_start, line_end}, cf. FSZero b369c99). That is a priority inversion: two p1 engine beads are blocked on a p2 hub decision. This bead pulls the decision out of b3l so it can land independently of the capability-negotiation work.

Deliverables:
1. Decide and document canonical policy per dimension in the hub contract.
2. Encode it in zero-ref as the default, so engines cannot silently pick differently.
3. Extend the golden-vector fixture with clamp and strict cases at the boundary.
4. State whether the capability descriptor must advertise the policy, and if so add it to the conformance schema.

Fixture v2 includes canonical clamp and strict override boundary vectors. docs/zeroref.md states policy is fixed by ZeroRef v1 and not separately capability-negotiated. title: GraphZero declares mutation "store-only", a value the contract does not define
description:
Found by the first live conformance run after the harness was repaired (ZeroStack 2241b75). G7 limits and G8 mutation both FAIL against GraphZero for the same reason.

CONTRACT.md section 2 defines exactly three mutation values and pins gz:
  | GraphZero | gz | readonly |
  readonly: same rejection behavior as denied, and the substrate additionally
  declares that no mutating substrate operations exist in CodeMode. Read-only
  metadata/ref writes needed to store execution records are not domain mutation.

GraphZero declares a fourth value instead:
  crates/graphzero-query/src/codemode/discovery.rs:33   "mutation": "store-only"
  crates/graphzero-query/src/codemode/discovery.rs:129  "mutation_surface": "store-only"
  crates/graphzero-query/tests/codemode_e2e.rs:661      asserts "store-only"
with the inline rationale "remember/reserve/index mutate GraphZero's own store".

Both sides have a real argument:
- The contract's readonly clause already carves out "read-only metadata/ref writes needed to store execution records", but remember/reserve/index are more than execution bookkeeping; they are caller-initiated writes to GraphZero's store. Calling that readonly is arguably a lie.
- Equally, the contract is normative and enumerates three values. An engine unilaterally inventing a fourth is exactly the drift the conformance suite exists to catch, and any consumer switching on mutation will hit an unknown variant.

Note the vocabulary ALSO drifts inside GraphZero: the CodeMode surface says "store-only" (hyphen) while the operation ABI says "store_only" (underscore) at operation_abi/digest.rs:64 and operation_abi/vectors.rs:76. Whatever is decided, one spelling.

This needs a contract owner, not a guess. Two coherent resolutions:
A. Add store-only to CONTRACT.md section 2 as a fourth value with defined semantics (which operations may write, what a consumer must assume), repin gz to it, and update the conformance schema + harness validator. Pick one spelling.
B. Declare readonly is correct because GraphZero's writes are store-internal and not domain mutation, and change GraphZero to declare readonly.

Blocks a passing gz attestation, so it blocks zerostack-conformance-refresh-ci-30a deliverable 4 (reconcile the GraphZero closed-but-unproven state). Related: zerostack-hix.

title: GraphZero has a second canonical-JSON implementation off zero-abi
description:
Undetected drift, no bead in any repo before this one.

GraphZero/crates/graphzero-pack/src/manifest.rs:85 defines its own unsigned_canonical_json. GraphZero already re-exports zero_abi canonical JSON elsewhere (crates/graphzero-query/src/operation_abi/schema.rs re-exports zero_abi canonical_json, canonical_schema_json, normalize_schema, schema_diff, and digest.rs:53,58 call zero_abi contract_digest*), so this one function is a parallel implementation of the single most drift-forbidden primitive in the stack.

Canonical JSON feeds the contract digest. If the pack manifest hashes bytes that zero-abi would encode differently, pack manifests and contract digests disagree about identity, and the disagreement is silent because both sides produce valid-looking hashes.

Deliverables:
1. Confirm whether unsigned_canonical_json is byte-identical to zero_abi canonical_json today. Differential test over the zero-abi fixture corpus plus pack manifest fixtures.
2. If identical, delete it and call zero-abi.
3. If not identical, that is a live digest bug: record which manifests were hashed with the divergent encoder before replacing it.
4. Add a hub-side guard so a second canonical-JSON implementation cannot reappear unnoticed.

Related: tokenzero-hks0 (canonical-JSON digest hardening against zero-abi), tokenzero-ghv7 (contract digest depends on registry declaration order).

STALE - all four deliverables already landed. Verified by executing them against CURRENT code, not by reading commit messages.

D1 (confirm whether unsigned_canonical_json is byte-identical to zero_abi canonical_json, via differential test): DONE and the answer is NO, they diverge. GraphZero 41170ab 'test(pack): prove the canonical-JSON divergence against zero-abi' adds crates/graphzero-pack/tests/canonical_json_drift.rs with 4 tests: manifest_encoder_emits_declaration_order_not_sorted_order, the_two_encoders_disagree_on_bytes (asserts different bytes but semantically equal after reparse), the_two_encoders_produce_different_digests, manifest_encoding_is_deterministic_and_blanks_the_signature.

D2 (if identical, delete it): NOT APPLICABLE - D1 proved non-identity.

D3 (if not identical, that is a live digest bug; record which manifests were hashed with the divergent encoder before replacing it): correctly SPLIT OUT rather than done here, because replacing the encoder is digest- AND signature-invalidating: unsigned_canonical_json is both the digest input (digest_sha256) and the exact ed25519-signed payload (graphzero-pack/src/sign.rs:9 sign, :16 verify). That migration is zerostack-t76, which is open and carries the manifest-recording item plus the schema-version bump and the v1 verification policy. Closing 881 does not lose D3; t76 owns it.

D4 (hub-side guard so a second canonical-JSON implementation cannot reappear unnoticed): DONE. conformance/scripts/check_canonical_json_impls.py walks all four checkouts for functions matching a canonical/json name regex, allows only zero-abi paths plus test/bench-local normalizers, and carries an explicit KNOWN_EXCEPTIONS map with the ONE tracked divergence keyed to its bead (graphzero-pack/src/manifest.rs unsigned_canonical_json -> zerostack-t76). Wired into .github/workflows/ci.yml job 'drift-guards', which no-ops with ::warning when engine checkouts are absent rather than falsely passing.

MUTATION-VERIFIED (this session): planted /tmp/fakeengine/crates/foo/src/lib.rs containing 'fn my_canonical_json'. The guard FAILED with exit 1 and named the file and function. Baseline run over the real checkouts: exit 0, '1132 files, 1 tracked divergence(s), 0 new'. So the gate detects a new implementation and is not vacuously passing.

Note the bead's own ordering constraint is satisfied: t76 says 'do NOT start until deliverable 4 of the parent lands' - D4 has landed, so t76 is now unblocked.

No code changed by me; verified-and-closed. Tree clean apart from pre-existing .beads/issues.jsonl export churn.

comments.author: QuietSummit
comments.text:
Deliverable 1 DONE, and the answer is NO: the two encoders are not byte-identical.

Evidence: GraphZero 41170ab adds crates/graphzero-pack/tests/canonical_json_drift.rs, 4 tests, all passing on spark via rch.

Root cause is narrower than the bead assumed. unsigned_canonical_json (graphzero-pack/src/manifest.rs:85) is plain serde_json::to_string over #[derive(Serialize)] on UnsignedPackManifestRef, so it emits DECLARATION order. zero_abi::canonical_json (ZeroStack crates/zero-abi/src/schema.rs:33) emits SORTED keys recursively. Both produce valid JSON that parses to an equal Value; only a hashing consumer can see the difference. So this is deliverable 3 (a live digest divergence), NOT deliverable 2 (identical, safe to delete).

Blast radius, why I did NOT migrate in that commit: unsigned_canonical_json feeds digest_sha256 and is the exact payload ed25519-signed at sign.rs:9 and verified at sign.rs:16. Switching encoders changes every pack manifest digest AND invalidates every existing signature. That needs a recorded migration with a schema_version bump, not a drive-by.

Also note graphzero-pack did not depend on zero-abi at all (only graphzero-query did), which is how this went undetected. Added zero-abi as a dev-dependency so the gate exists without coupling the shipped crate.

Remaining: deliverable 3 (record which manifests were hashed with the divergent encoder) and deliverable 4 (hub-side guard against a third canonical-JSON impl). Filing those separately as migration work.

title: conformance harness must test ONE installed surface, not a dual-surface binary
description:
The conformance harness cannot run against ANY current engine. This is worse than the staleness recorded in zerostack-conformance-refresh-ci-30a: the suite is not merely out of date, its core process model contradicts what all three engines now enforce.

HARNESS ASSUMPTION (conformance/src/lib.rs):
  :885  McpClient::spawn(bin, mode, timeout) runs Command::new(bin).arg("--mode={mode}")
  :477  check_exposure spawns ONE binary as --mode=codemode
  :487  ...then spawns the SAME binary as --mode=mcp
  G1 "exposure" is defined as: the codemode surface exposes exactly the codemode tools, AND the mcp surface exposes none of them. That check is only meaningful if one artifact can serve both.

ENGINE REALITY (verified by direct invocation, 2026-07-25, all three release binaries):

  TokenZero target/release/tokenzero-mcp --mode=codemode
    exit 101: "artifact is locked to surface 'mcp'; refused --mode=codemode.
    Install tokenzero-codemode for the CodeMode catalog (mutually exclusive)."

  FSZero target/release/fszero --mode=codemode
    exit 2: "packaging shim has no surface runtime compiled in. Install fszero-mcp
    or fszero-codemode (selection is immutable), or invoke that artifact directly.
    Do not pass --mode= to a dual-capable process - dual surfaces are forbidden."

  GraphZero target/release/graphzero --mode=codemode
    exit 1: "the compatibility shim does not host MCP/CodeMode servers. Install
    graphzero-codemode (selected surface) or rebuild the matching single-surface artifact."

TokenZero enforces this at COMPILE time, not just runtime: building --features "surface-mcp,surface-codemode" hits
  compile_error!("tokenzero surfaces are mutually exclusive (tokenzero-irx9.3): enable exactly one of feature surface-mcp or surface-codemode - never both.")
So a dual-surface tokenzero artifact cannot be produced at all. The harness's G1 is unsatisfiable by construction.

This explains why the reports froze on 2026-07-01: that is approximately when single-surface artifacts landed, and nobody could run the suite afterward. The 23 committed reports attest to a binary shape that no longer exists.

REQUIRED CHANGE:
RunConfig must take a surface pair, not one path. Suggested:
  --codemode-bin <path> --mcp-bin <path>
with --bin kept as a back-compat alias meaning "same artifact for both", which is now only true for test fixtures like the built-in fake substrate.

G1 exposure then becomes a cross-ARTIFACT check: the codemode artifact exposes exactly the codemode tool set, and the mcp artifact exposes none of it. That is the same invariant the check was always trying to express, and it stays meaningful under single-surface packaging. It arguably gets STRONGER, since surface separation is now enforced by the build rather than by a runtime flag.

Also fix while in here (found during the same investigation):
- Reports record substrate_binary as an absolute authoring-machine path, e.g. "/Users/<name>/AI/tokenzero/target/release/tokenzero". That is a local-layout leak in a public repo. Record basenames. Overlaps zerostack-9g4.
- ReportFile has no engine revision field, so no report can be tied to the code it attests to. Contract and checker for this already landed: conformance/reports/ATTESTATION.md and conformance/scripts/check_freshness.py.

BLOCKS: zerostack-conformance-refresh-ci-30a deliverable 1 (re-run the suite against current engine HEADs). 30a deliverables 2 and 3 (CI wiring, freshness contract) are already done and do not depend on this.
close_reason: Fixed and pushed as a25c523. Harness now models one artifact + one Surface (bin/surface), infers surface from filename, refuses to guess on the bare shim, and G1 checks that the artifact serves its own surface AND refuses the opposite. G2-G10 only run against a codemode artifact. Verified against installed graphzero-codemode: G1 now PASSES (previously failed only because the harness demanded a second artifact that must not exist); G4/G5/G10 pass; remaining failures are the real contract divergences tracked as mpi and g25. Workspace fmt+clippy -D warnings+tests green.

comments.author: QuietSummit
comments.text:
Harness now runs against real engines (ZeroStack 2241b75). First live gz run produced ACTIONABLE findings, and they point at the HARNESS being wrong, not the engine.

G2/G6 "invalid CodeMode ref": GraphZero emits
  gz://codemode/execution/cm___exec_1784970306329-20532-0-2afa6c5e5632
The harness ref regex (conformance/src/lib.rs:64) is
  ^{ns}://(blob/[0-9a-f]{64}|codemode/execution/[^/]+/(code|steps|telemetry|result|error))$
which REQUIRES a trailing /code|/steps|/telemetry|/result|/error segment. The bare execution root ref has no suffix and cannot match. GraphZero also emits all four suffixed refs alongside it, so the engine looks correct and the regex looks too strict. Needs a contract decision: is the bare execution root a legal ref? If yes, make the suffix optional.

G5 errors, G10 sandbox: harness reports "case did not return structured error", but the payloads clearly ARE structured, with correct kinds:
  validation -> kind "validation"
  sandbox    -> kind "sandbox"   ("network/fetch denied")
  runtime    -> kind "runtime"
  substrate  -> kind "substrate"
  policy     -> kind "policy"    ("CodeMode is read-only; mutating JS binding 'edit' is unavailable")
Every one carries isError true, structuredContent.error.{kind,message,retryable}, and error_ref. So extract_json_payload is failing to find them. GraphZero wraps them in a content[] entry of type "structuredContent" AND repeats them at top-level structuredContent; the harness likely only looks at content[0].text and tries to parse it as JSON, but content[0].text here is the human-readable ack line, not JSON. Harness bug.

G7 limits: "invalid mutation \"store-only\"". CONTRACT.md section 2 admits only allowed|denied|readonly, and pins gz to readonly. GraphZero declares store-only. This one may be a real engine or contract divergence: either GraphZero should declare readonly, or the contract needs a fourth value defined. Do not guess, needs a decision.

G1 exposure: "server exited while waiting for initialize response" for the mcp side. graphzero (the shim) is not the mcp-surface artifact; there is probably a graphzero-mcp that was not built. Need the right artifact before G1 means anything.

Recommend splitting: harness ref-regex + payload-extraction fixes are one bead, the mutation vocabulary question is another, since the second needs a contract owner.

comments.author: QuietSummit
comments.text:
CORRECTION. My first fix was also wrong, in the same direction as the original bug.

I replaced "one binary, two --mode= spawns" with "--codemode-bin plus --mcp-bin", i.e. two artifacts present at once. That still assumes both surfaces exist side by side. They do not. The product rule is EITHER/OR at INSTALL time:

  crates/tokenzero-install/src/packaging.rs:3
    "Product rule: users install **one** of tokenzero-mcp or tokenzero-codemode
     from the same revision and shared core. The installer writes one client
     registration and replaces any prior surface. Dual catalog / dual mode
     startup fails closed."
  packaging.rs:13
    "The tokenzero name is a compatibility shim / selected symlink only -
     never a dual-surface binary."

So you install ONE surface. Requiring both artifacts describes a machine state that is not allowed to exist, and on a normally-installed host the second path simply is not there. My version would have failed for the wrong reason.

Correct model, now implemented:
  RunConfig { bin, surface }        one artifact, one surface
  --bin <path> --surface codemode|mcp
  surface inferred from the filename (<name>-codemode / <name>-mcp) so the
  common case needs no flag. The bare shim is NOT guessed: it is a selected
  symlink, so an unrecognizable name is a hard error rather than a default,
  because silently running the wrong surface's checks yields misleading
  evidence.

G1 exposure is now a property of the ONE artifact under test, checked two ways:
  1. it serves the tool set its surface implies (codemode artifact exposes
     exactly the codemode tools; mcp artifact exposes none of them), and
  2. it REFUSES the opposite surface. A single-surface artifact that also
     answers as its opposite is precisely the dual catalog the product rule
     forbids, so serving it is the failure and refusing it is the pass.
That second half is the invariant that actually protects the separation, and neither the original harness nor my first fix tested it.

G2-G10 exercise CodeMode execution semantics, so they now only run against a codemode artifact. Against an mcp artifact there is no execute_code to drive; reporting those as failures was a category error.

VERIFIED against the installed gz codemode artifact:
  bin: graphzero-codemode
  G1 exposure PASS      <- was FAIL "server exited while waiting for initialize"
  G4 leak-proof PASS
  G5 errors PASS
  G10 sandbox-denial PASS
  G2/G3/G6/G9 FAIL -> zerostack-mpi (no execution_id, no inline telemetry)
  G7/G8 FAIL       -> zerostack-g25 (mutation "store-only")
G1 was only ever failing because the harness insisted on a second artifact that must not exist. The remaining failures are the real contract divergences, unchanged.

Also verified the shim refuses to be guessed:
  --bin .../graphzero
  -> Error: cannot tell which surface "graphzero" serves; pass --surface codemode or --surface mcp

title: apply the beads-export scrub and privacy gates to TokenZero, FSZero, and GraphZero
description:
Follow-up to zerostack-sg3, which built and proved the shared scrub but deliberately applied it only to the hub.

scripts/scrub_beads_export.py in the hub (ZeroStack eb2b7b7) works cross-repo. Run from the hub against each engine's export it reports:
  TokenZero  248 record(s) carry absolute host paths
  FSZero     310 record(s)
  GraphZero  846 record(s)

All three .beads/issues.jsonl files are tracked, and TokenZero is public, so this is the same exposure as the hub had: username and directory layout on every issue record via br's source_repo_path stamp, plus absolute paths quoted in descriptions and comments.

WHY THIS WAS NOT DONE IN THE SAME PASS
Scrubbing rewrites 248/310/846 records, which is a very large diff in each repo. At the time of filing, other sessions had substantial uncommitted work in those trees (I lost my own uncommitted TokenZero edits to a concurrent operation earlier in this session, see the note on zerostack-wth). Landing a whole-file rewrite of a tracked, actively-synced file underneath another agent is a good way to cause a conflict or destroy work. It should be done when those trees are quiet.

DELIVERABLES
1. Run the scrub in TokenZero, FSZero, and GraphZero, one commit per repo, when the tree is quiet and the other sessions have committed.
2. Verify integrity the same way the hub was verified, and do not skip this: record count unchanged, id order unchanged, per-record key sets unchanged, and only source_repo_path, description, and comments differing. The hub check caught nothing wrong, but a silent field loss across 846 records would be very hard to notice later.
3. Copy or reference the two gates into each engine repo's CI, since a scrub with no gate will simply rot the moment the next br sync runs. The hub runs both check_no_host_paths.py and scrub_beads_export.py --check in a privacy job.
4. Add the scrub to each repo's documented br sync recipe, as was done in the hub AGENTS.md, so it is a required step rather than folklore.

Note the ordering constraint: the scrub must run AFTER br sync --flush-only and BEFORE git add, because br rewrites the export from SQLite on every sync and will reintroduce the absolute path each time. A one-time scrub without the recipe change and the CI gate accomplishes nothing durable.

Decide whether to vendor a copy of the script per repo or reference the hub copy. A copy per repo is more robust, since the engine repos should not require a hub checkout to pass their own CI, but then the four copies must be kept in sync.

Refs zerostack-sg3, zerostack-9g4.

title: shell repo-inventory heuristic mangles compound commands, shredding file content into sample_paths
description:
Hit repeatedly while doing conformance work on 2026-07-25. Not a blocker, but it costs a wasted round trip almost every time and will do the same to every future agent.

zero.token.shell wraps some commands in a "structured (repo inventory command)" policy that reformats output into a repo_inventory block with files_seen/dirs_seen/sample_paths. That is useful for a bare ls. It is actively wrong when the command is a compound shell line whose real payload is on stdout.

Concrete case:
  zero.token.shell("ls /tmp/qs/probe-reports/ && cat /tmp/qs/probe-reports/$(ls ... | head -1)")
The heuristic saw a leading ls, classified the whole thing as repo inventory, and then rendered the JSON report I actually wanted as "sample_paths" entries, one array element per LINE of JSON:
  - gz-2026-07-25-050508.json
  - "contract_version": "1.0",
  - "invalid CodeMode ref \"gz://...\"",
  - "name": "ctx.step",
So the file content was shredded into a path list. Every line got treated as a filesystem path. I had to re-fetch via the combined_ref to read it.

Second case, same root cause: an ls of two paths where the second does not exist returns exit 1 and the stderr line
  ls: /path: No such file or directory
appears as a sample_paths ENTRY, alongside real -rwxr-xr-x lines. A consumer parsing sample_paths as paths gets an error message as a path.

Suggested fix, roughly in order of value:
1. Only apply the inventory policy when the command is a SINGLE listing command with no &&, ||, ;, or | and no command substitution. A compound line should fall through to plain capture.
2. Never route stderr into sample_paths. Inventory is a stdout concept.
3. When the policy is applied, still make the raw stdout trivially reachable; today combined_ref works but it is a second round trip that the caller did not know they needed until they saw mangled output.

Impact is mild but constant: it silently corrupts the shape of data you asked for, and it does so most often when an agent is reading evidence files, which is exactly when fidelity matters. Filed rather than worked around, per the standing instruction to report ZeroStack problems as beads.
close_reason: Independently re-verified on the live origin-main binary TokenZero 78a9a12 from a fresh session. Compound commands with a leading listing are no longer classified as repo inventory and return the payload verbatim. Listing a real and a missing path still classifies as inventory but sample paths now contains only the real entry, with the stderr diagnostic excluded. Bare single listings are still classified as inventory as intended. Fixed in TokenZero 7bada5e.

title: TokenZero shared store has no project namespacing: unrelated projects collide on one path
description:
This is the only divergence in the store-root triplicate that puts DIFFERENT objects at the SAME path, rather than the same object at different paths.

TokenZero/crates/tokenzero-engine/src/workspace.rs:106-124 always resolves to <store>/tokenzero/recovery-cache.json with no project key. N unrelated projects sharing one ZEROSTACK_STORE_ROOT all write that same file. workspace.rs:203-216 only emits a store_project_mismatch warning in the resolution report; nothing prevents the collision.

The other two namespace correctly when the store is outside the repo:
- GraphZero: <store>/projects/<project_key>/graphzero/ (zerostack_store.rs:114-123)
- FSZero: <store>/fszero/repos/<sid>/ (zerostack_store.rs:56-62)

Recommended canonical shape is GraphZeros: <root>/projects/<key>/<engine>, with the key being 16 lowercase hex chars of sha256 over the absolutized root path, no prefix. FSZeros sid- prefix belongs at the directory level, not in the key; keeping prefixes means no engine can predict another engines shard directory (FSZero sid-<16hex> = 20 chars vs GraphZero <16hex> = 16).

Also: key input bytes diverge. FSZero uses fs::canonicalize or the path as-given without absolutizing (zerostack_store.rs:100-105); GraphZero absolutizes against cwd when the path does not exist (store/path_safety.rs:35-45). For a nonexistent relative repo_root, FSZero hashes "rel/path" and GraphZero hashes "<cwd>/rel/path", producing different keys for the same repo.

Migration: TokenZero gains namespacing, <pin>/tokenzero/recovery-cache.json moves to <pin>/projects/<key>/tokenzero/recovery-cache.json. FSZero moves fszero/repos/<sid>/ to projects/<key>/fszero/. GraphZero unchanged.

Anti-collision gate: two distinct roots sharing one pin must resolve to different engine dirs. That test fails against TokenZero today.

Part of zerostack-sce part B.

title: GraphZero execute_code envelope lacks execution_id and inline telemetry the contract requires
description:
Found by the first live conformance run after the harness was repaired (ZeroStack 2241b75, plus the payload-extraction fix). G2 refs, G3 telemetry, G6 ctx.step, and G9 coalescing all FAIL against GraphZero, and unlike G5/G10 these are NOT harness bugs.

CONTRACT.md section on {ns}_execute_code specifies the success envelope:
  { "ack": "C",
    "execution_id": "cm://exec/1782920000000-012345abcdef",
    "refs": { "code":..., "steps":..., "telemetry":..., "result":... },
    "telemetry": { "kind": "codemode.execute", "status": "ok", "logical_ops":...,
                   "physical_ops":..., "wall_ms":..., ... } }

GraphZero actually returns (verified by direct stdio invocation of
target/release/graphzero-codemode, plan "return 1+1;", form js):
  structuredContent top-level keys: ["ack", "ref", "refs", "value"]
  ack   = "ok gz2 96% t:q:7149bee088e3c5a9"
  ref   = "gz://codemode/execution/cm___exec_1784970487262-50629-0-aae1dac37219/result"
  refs  = [ gz://blob/<64hex>, .../<id>, .../<id>/steps, .../<id>/telemetry, .../<id>/result ]
  value = { ack: "C", ref: "gz://blob/...", value: 2 }

Three concrete divergences:

1. NO execution_id field. The contract wants a top-level execution_id of the form cm://exec/<id>. GraphZero embeds the id only inside ref/refs strings, spelled cm___exec_1784970487262-50629-0-aae1dac37219 (triple underscore, not cm://exec/). A consumer cannot read the execution id without string-parsing a ref, and the id spelling itself differs from the contract's.

2. NO inline telemetry object. The contract wants telemetry inline in the response. GraphZero returns only a gz://.../telemetry REF, requiring a second round trip. This is defensible as a ref-first design and may well be the better shape, but it is not what the contract says, and G3/G9 cannot pass as written. Note G9 coalescing specifically needs telemetry counters to observe batching, so a ref-only telemetry makes that check impossible without an expand step the harness does not do.

3. ack is not "C". The contract shows ack "C" on success; GraphZero returns "ok gz2 96% t:q:<hash>" at the envelope level and puts ack "C" one level down in value. So the contract's shape appears at value, not at the top.

Note GraphZero looks INTERNALLY consistent and arguably richer than the contract; this reads as the contract having been written against an older or different envelope and never reconciled, rather than as a regression. That is exactly the "closed-but-unproven" state zerostack-conformance-refresh-ci-30a flagged: GraphZero closed zeroref-v1-shared-cas-1ghi.8/.9 as done while its own evidence file stayed pending.

Needs a contract owner decision, same as zerostack-g25:
A. The contract is normative and GraphZero must add execution_id and inline telemetry.
B. The ref-first envelope is correct and CONTRACT.md plus the harness must be updated to match, with telemetry expansion added to G3/G9.

Do not guess. Whichever way it goes, TokenZero and FSZero must be checked for the same divergence before a shared answer is written down, since the contract is supposed to be cross-engine.

Related: zerostack-hix (harness), zerostack-g25 (mutation vocabulary), zerostack-conformance-refresh-ci-30a (parent).

root (/Users/aditya). A clean checkout at /tmp/ixka-clean produced, from rch/src/hook.rs:1691:

2. 'rch diagnose --dry-run' on the SAME path reports "Would offload: YES (compilation command

command produced "[RCH] remote spark-1672" with real offload and artifact retrieval.

canonical root <root>") rather than "remote execution failed", and 'rch diagnose' must report
NO for a path it will refuse, rather than YES.

title: CAS temp-file reapers are mutually blind: each engine leaks the others temp files forever
description:
Three temp-file naming schemes and two mutually exclusive reap predicates, so abandoned temps from a crashed publisher are never cleaned by a different engine sharing the store.

Names:
- hub ZeroStack/crates/zero-store/src/cas.rs:197 and GraphZero .../shared_cas.rs:141 -> .tmp-<hash[..8]>-<pid>-<seq>
- TokenZero .../shared_cas.rs:87 -> .tmp-<hash64>-<nanos>-<n>.blob
- FSZero src/core/cas.rs:231-238 -> <hash64>.<pid>.<seq>.tmp

Reap predicates:
- hub cas.rs:300-320 and GraphZero :251 match PREFIX ".tmp-", age >= 3600s
- FSZero cas.rs:281-291 matches SUFFIX ".tmp", age >= 900s
- TokenZero has no reaper at all

So FSZero never reaps hub or GraphZero or TokenZero temps (no .tmp suffix), and hub and GraphZero never reap FSZero temps (no .tmp- prefix). On a shared store root the leak is permanent and grows with every crashed publish.

Fix: one reaper in zero-store that recognizes all three historical shapes. Equality gate: a test that plants all three shapes and asserts the unified reaper removes them when stale and none of them when young.

title: store-root resolution: FSZero inverts precedence and has no shared-store opt-in gate
description:
Two engines resolve the same repo to different store roots, so a single logical store silently splits.

FSZero/src/core/zerostack_store.rs:20-27 checks the env pin FIRST and has no opt-in gate:
  if let Some(v) = env(ZEROSTACK_STORE_ROOT).or(ZERO_STACK_STORE_ROOT) { return Some(...) }
  let candidate = repo_root.join(".zerostack"); if candidate.is_dir() { Some(candidate) } else { None }

TokenZero/crates/tokenzero-engine/src/workspace.rs:77-95 and GraphZero/crates/graphzero-store/src/store/zerostack_store.rs:91-112 both check local .zerostack FIRST, then require a shared-store opt-in before honoring the pin.

Consequences:
- Repo with .zerostack present plus ZEROSTACK_STORE_ROOT=/shared and no opt-in: FSZero writes /shared/fszero/repos/<sid>/, TokenZero and GraphZero write <repo>/.zerostack/.
- Bare ZEROSTACK_STORE_ROOT with no .zerostack: FSZero honors it, the other two ignore it.
- FSZERO_SHARED_STORE does not exist anywhere in FSZero source. Only a doc mention of ZEROSTACK_SHARED_STORE at FSZero/docs/design/zeroref-v1-annex.md:152. Adding it is a new surface, not a rename.

Recommended canonical behavior, 2 of 3 majority: local .zerostack wins over the pin, and the pin requires opt-in. The local marker is an explicit per-repo declaration; a process-global env is ambient and a stray value in an agent harness should not relocate one engines store.

Migration: FSZero only. Repos with both .zerostack and a pin move <pin>/fszero/{store.sqlite3,repos/<sid>/store.sqlite3} to <repo>/.zerostack/fszero/store.sqlite3. FSZero already has the machinery at src/core/store_migration.rs:87-100. With a bare ungated pin, FSZero returns to <repo>/.fszero/store.sqlite3, which looks like data loss to existing users, so ship FSZERO_SHARED_STORE plus a one-shot migration that adopts the old ungated location.

Part of zerostack-sce part B.
close_reason: FSZero now uses the two-of-three canonical order. src/core/zerostack_store.rs gained resolve_store_root_with_env with the same rule TokenZero (workspace.rs:79) and GraphZero (zerostack_store.rs:91) already share: local .zerostack wins, then the pin, and only when opted in. Added FSZERO_SHARED_STORE / ZEROSTACK_SHARED_STORE with the same truthy set (1|on|true|yes, trimmed, case-insensitive) and the same empty-pin filter. Commit 3093e45 in FSZero; docs corrected in a3fc479 (shared-cas.md named the old precedence outright; README.md and mcp.md implied a bare pin sufficed). Migration shipped as required, because the precedence fix alone strands data in exactly the two cases the bead names: repo with both .zerostack and a pin, and a bare ungated pin (which now falls back to legacy .fszero and would look like data loss). adopt_superseded_store runs from prepare_repo_store before the DB is opened, using superseded_store_root to name where the OLD resolver would have looked, and moves the DB there to the location the new resolver names. Safety properties, each pinned by a test AND mutation-verified by breaking it and confirming the specific test goes red: never overwrites (conflict reported, both DBs preserved, since merging two live databases is not a decision it can make); copy-then-remove rather than rename, because the pin is usually on another filesystem where rename fails EXDEV; staged into the destination dir then renamed, so a crash leaves the untouched source or a complete destination, never a half-written DB; -wal/-shm move with the DB, since a stranded -wal holds committed-but-uncheckpointed transactions; inert when source and destination coincide. Verified: 11 new tests in tests/zerostack_store_pi1.rs pass. Reverting the resolver to the pin-first ungated order turns all 6 precedence tests red including the bead's exact scenario. precedence_matches_the_canonical_cross_engine_table asserts all 8 combinations of (local, pin, opt-in) so a future one-off tweak to any branch surfaces as a diff rather than silent drift. Suite-wide the failure set is IDENTICAL before and after: 9 failures, all pre-existing (lib codemode accounting x2, batch_ops, cas, cas_migration x2, child_root x5), confirmed by stashing the change and rerunning the same four suites. No new rustfmt drift.

title: CRITICAL TOCTOU: CAS publish never takes the GC coordination lock, so GC unlinks live objects
description:
A publisher and the garbage collector can interleave such that GC unlinks an object a publisher just republished or is about to reference. Publish returns Ok(hash), contains(hash) was true, and the object file is then gone. Later reads are NotFound, not Corruption, so this is silent data loss plus a dangling reference from a committed root. Nothing panics and the GC report claims a clean Collect.

Root cause: publish takes no coordination lock in any engine, and the sweepers pre-unlink recheck inspects only gc/** metadata, never the object identity or mtime.

TokenZero/crates/tokenzero-recovery/src/shared_cas.rs:
  :77-109   publish() - no lock acquired
  :1134     run_gc() acquires GcCoordLock
  :1213     per-hash recheck: load_mark_state again (metadata only)
  :1217     cas.remove_object(hash) -> unlink
  :178-201  remove_object re-stats only "regular file, not symlink"
  :1079-1092 GcCoordLock::acquire, taken by run_gc and the three record publishers, never by publish

Interleaving (GC left, publisher right):
  1 acquire lock
  2 load_mark_state: h absent from roots/pins/leases, uncertain=false
  3 build_dry_run_report reads h mtime -> age >= min_age -> Collect
  4 write report, persist progress
  5                         publish(bytes) for the same h, no lock. dest exists -> verify_existing -> Ok(h). No mtime touch, no pin, no lease.
  6                         caller records h into an in-flight root/manifest; new snapshot not yet published
  7 recheck load_mark_state: still no reference -> passes
  8 remove_object(h) -> unlink
  9                         publisher commits the root referencing h
  11                        later resolve(h) -> NotFound

Variant B: a fresh publish lands a new inode via create_new + rename for a hash already listed Collect, and step 8 deletes it. min_age is defeated twice: the age came from the pre-rename or pre-republish inode, and remove_object never re-stats mtime.

Per-engine:
- TokenZero: vulnerable and is the deleter. Publish lockless, recheck metadata-only, unlink without identity or mtime recheck and without quarantine.
- FSZero: vulnerable, partially mitigated. It holds an exclusive advisory lock for the whole sweep (src/core/cas.rs:249-251) but put/put_prehashed never acquire it (:146-188), so its own window is identical. touch_blob on existing-put and on get (:161,:197) plus a 7-day grace (:53) reduce exposure but do not close it: a blob older than the grace that gains a new reference without any put or get is still deleted, and TokenZero GC ignores mtime once min_age is satisfied.
- GraphZero: cannot cause it, never deletes (crates/graphzero-store/src/store/gc_roots.rs:11-13), but is a victim. SharedCas::put takes no lock, so TokenZero run_gc on a shared root can unlink a GraphZero object.
- No engine mitigates it fully.

Fix, once, in the hub: one advisory lock at <store_root>/gc/coordinator.lock. Publishers take it Shared across hash -> dest check -> rename -> protection record write; the sweeper takes it Exclusive across mark -> report -> recheck -> quarantine/unlink. remove_object and quarantine_object accept a &StoreLock rather than acquiring one, so the sweeper cannot forget it. Single lock means no lock order and no cycle; both acquisitions are deadline-bounded; kernel releases on process death so no stale reclaim is needed.

Regression test must be deterministic via a GcHooks::before_unlink seam plus channels, not timing: block GC between recheck and unlink, then assert a concurrent protected publish blocks (proof the shared lock is excluded), release, and assert get_verified returns the bytes. Pre-fix behavior is the exact inverse.

Implemented as part of zerostack-sce wave 1.
close_reason: Fixed in all three engines. Root cause confirmed against source: publish/put took no coordination lock in any engine, while only the sweeper held one, so a reference established between the sweeper's metadata-only recheck and its unlink was invisible to it. Fix is the single-lock design from the bead: publishers take the coordinator lock SHARED across hash -> dest check -> rename, the sweeper keeps it EXCLUSIVE across mark -> report -> recheck -> unlink. One lock, so no lock order and no cycle; kernel releases on death; verified nothing acquires it while already holding it, so no self-deadlock. TokenZero (commit 3097dac, the deleter): GcCoordLock gained acquire_shared, publish() takes it, and remove_object() now requires a &GcCoordLock so a sweeper cannot forget it; added a before_unlink hook so the regression pins GC at the exact window via channels rather than timing. FSZero (commit 03795cf): put_prehashed holds the existing .gc.lock shared; gc() already used try_lock so it fails closed with cas_gc_busy. GraphZero (commit 126e031): put_with_limit holds <root>/gc/coordinator.lock shared, the same file TokenZero's sweeper takes, so the two engines coordinate on one lock; also tightened cas_writes_nothing_outside_the_object_namespace to assert the blob namespace exactly plus a one-entry allowlist outside it. Every regression was mutation-tested: removing the shared acquisition turns each red with the exact pre-fix symptom. tokenzero-recovery 188+ pass, fszero core::cas 3/3, graphzero shared_cas_contract 13/13; clippy and rustfmt clean on all touched files. Two pre-existing unrelated failures were confirmed independent by stashing and reproducing at HEAD: fszero codemode::host accounting tests, and graphzero amdahl_cold_index_breakdown (a timing-fraction assertion, reproduced 5/5 at baseline).

title: wave 1.5: CAS publish/GC core + .zerostack store-root resolution into zero-store
description: Two drift-forbidden pieces move into zero-store. (A) CAS internals: TZ shared_cas.rs (1,485 LOC incl. zerostack.cas-gc.v1 GC), FZ core/cas.rs (341), GZ store CAS — shared publish protocol (temp+fsync+rename), object verify, and the GC state machine live once; fixes the omega-math CRITICAL TOCTOU (GC unlinking concurrently republished objects; publish never takes the GC lock) exactly once instead of three times. (B) Store-root resolution: TZ engine/workspace.rs (~250), FZ core/zerostack_store.rs (137), GZ store/zerostack_store.rs (533) all reimplement .zerostack/ detection, ZEROSTACK_STORE_ROOT/ZERO_STACK_STORE_ROOT precedence, shared-store opt-in, and sha256 project-key namespacing — if these drift, engines put data in different places and interop silently breaks. Shared module owns layout + resolution; engines keep alias envs (TOKENZERO_SHARED_STORE etc.) as thin wrappers. TZ = PR, GZ/FZ direct. Equality gates: digest byte-identical per engine + store-path golden tests (same inputs resolve same paths before/after).

comments.author: aditya
comments.text:
Wave 1 part B landed, plus the publish side of part A.

Shipped in crates/zero-store:
- store_root.rs: one resolver for all three engines. Canonical rules, reconciling the three that had drifted: project-local .zerostack outranks the env pin; the pin requires shared-store opt-in; an exported-but-empty pin means unset; a pin outside the project is namespaced as <root>/projects/<key>/<engine>; the project key is 16 lowercase hex of sha256 over the absolutized root path with no prefix; the CAS is shared per store root and never project-namespaced. Engines pass only their own opt-in aliases, so precedence and truthiness live in one place. 21 tests, driven from the golden matrix, including the two gates the engines fail today: distinct projects never collide under one pin (TokenZero fails this, zerostack-ljx) and all three engines derive the same project key (FSZero fails this on its sid- prefix).
- gc_lock.rs: the single store coordination lock at <store_root>/gc/coordinator.lock. Publishers shared, sweeper exclusive. One lock means no lock order and no cycle, so deadlock freedom is structural. Acquisition is deadline-bounded so a wedged holder surfaces as a typed WouldBlock rather than a hang, and the kernel releases on process death so no stale reclaim is needed. The path is deliberately identical to TokenZeros existing GcCoordLock, and both fs4 and std map to flock on Unix, so a hub publisher and a not-yet-migrated TokenZero sweeper interoperate during the cutover.
- cas.rs: publish now runs under the shared guard, which is the publish half of the TOCTOU fix (zerostack-rhd). Added PutOutcome with a created flag, put_outcome, put_prehashed that re-derives and compares the digest so a wrong hash writes nothing, touch, list_objects, and remove_object plus quarantine_object which take a &StoreLock instead of acquiring one, so a sweeper cannot forget the guard. Dedup now refreshes mtime, since a dedup is a fresh reference and an age-based policy that never sees it collects a live object. The temp reaper recognizes all three historical engine shapes, closing the mutual blindness in zerostack-oh7. object_path no longer panics on short input.

Verification: zero-store 8 tests to 45. Workspace 60 to 100, all passing. zero-store is clippy-clean and fmt-clean. The publish/GC race has a deterministic regression test that parks a sweeper between its decision and its unlink using channel rendezvous, asserts a publish is excluded, then asserts the republished object is readable. No timing assumptions anywhere.

Empirically resolved an open question from the design analysis: on rustc 1.97.1 the std signatures are File::try_lock() -> Result<(), std::fs::TryLockError> and try_lock_shared() the same, not Result<bool>. Probed rather than assumed, so no new dependency was needed: fs4 is not required.

Remaining for this bead, the larger half of part A: port the zerostack.cas-gc.v1 state machine itself (records, mark, report, resumable sweep, epoch monotonicity, uncertainty policy) from TokenZero shared_cas.rs:296-1471 into a zero-store gc module, which needs serde promoted from dev-dependency to dependency. Until that lands the lock is in place but the sweeper still lives in TokenZero. Then the engine cutovers: TokenZero by PR, FSZero and GraphZero direct.

title: lossy elision is only flagged in a trailing footer, never inline at the cut point
description:
Two smaller ZeroStack surface issues found during conformance work on 2026-07-25, filed together since both are about output fidelity.

1. LOSSY COMPRESSION CAN DROP THE PAYLOAD WITH ONLY A FOOTER AS WARNING
Reading a conformance report through zero.token.shell returned a result tagged
  [mode=lossy lossy_policy_id=tokenzero.visible-compression.v1
   lossy_spans=[{description=omitted-bytes reason=visible-budget
   recovery_may_be_needed=true}]]
The visible text was truncated mid-value. The footer is honest, but it is at the END of a long block, so an agent that reads top-down and stops early will act on a partial JSON payload believing it is complete. When the omitted span falls inside a JSON document the remaining text is not even parseable, yet nothing marks the truncation point inline.
Suggested: mark the elision INLINE at the point it happens, e.g. a clear sentinel where bytes were dropped, so truncation is visible exactly where it matters rather than only in a trailing annotation. Bonus: when the payload is detected as JSON, prefer eliding whole values over cutting mid-token.

2. grep -A/-B THROUGH shell RETURNS A REF, NOT THE MATCH
  zero.token.shell("grep -n 'fn extract_json_payload' -A 30 file.rs")
returned only
  preview: 884:fn extract_json_payload(
i.e. the first matched line, with the -A 30 context available solely behind a second expand of the blob ref. Same for -B. The whole point of -A/-B is the surrounding context, so the one flag that makes grep useful is the one whose output does not survive. This turns a routine one-call code read into two calls, every time.
Suggested: when the command carries -A/-B/-C, treat the context lines as the payload and show them, since the caller has explicitly declared how much context they want.

Neither is a correctness bug in the engines; both are ZeroStack surface ergonomics that cost an extra round trip and, in case 1, risk silent misreads. Filed per the standing instruction to report ZeroStack problems as beads.

  The 30 lines of requested context were reachable only through a second expand of the blob ref.

After, the context comes back inline in one call:
  grep -n "fn substrate_label" -A 12 conformance/src/lib.rs

If it lands, rnv2 reopens, since a divergent copy of this string is precisely what made the visible-budget test fail P01-001 (test modelled a 14-token marker, real marker costs 33).

CURRENT BEHAVIOUR, read from the code
enforce_token_budget_with_ref keeps a prefix of whole lines, then appends the marker as a trailing line:
  out = prefix + "\n" + marker
It already does the thing rnv2 added: marker_tokens is subtracted from the budget before deciding what fits, and if the marker alone exceeds the budget, or nothing fits, the marker is returned alone as a correctness floor. So the accounting is sound. The defect in this bead is purely POSITIONAL: the annotation is always appended at the end, never placed where bytes were actually dropped.

Note the marker has two forms. With a recovery_ref it is a readable "... omitted by visible budget; expand REF ..." line; without one it is the machine-readable lossy declaration. Both are appended trailing, so both have this problem.

2. When the payload is detected as JSON, elide whole values instead of cutting mid-token, since a mid-token cut leaves text that will not parse.
3. Keep VISIBLE_BUDGET_LOSSY_DECLARATION as the single source of truth and preserve the marker-cost accounting rnv2 established, so P01-001 stays green.
Since truncation here is always a suffix cut, "inline at the cut point" and "trailing" coincide for the plain case; the real win is item 2 plus not losing the marker when a caller reads only the head of a long block.ZEOF

title: migrate pack manifest to zero-abi canonical JSON (digest+signature invalidating)
description:
Follow-up to zerostack-graphzero-canonical-json-drift-881, which PROVED the divergence (GraphZero 41170ab, 4 passing differential tests) but deliberately did not migrate.

GraphZero PackManifest::unsigned_canonical_json emits struct declaration order; zero_abi::canonical_json emits sorted keys. Different bytes, different SHA-256.

Migrating is not a cleanup because unsigned_canonical_json is BOTH the digest input (digest_sha256) and the exact ed25519-signed payload (graphzero-pack/src/sign.rs:9 sign, :16 verify). Switching encoders changes every pack manifest digest and invalidates every existing signature.

Required:
1. Bump MANIFEST_SCHEMA_VERSION so old and new manifests are distinguishable rather than silently incompatible.
2. Decide verification policy for already-signed v1 manifests: accept via the legacy encoder, or hard-fail and re-sign. Do not silently accept both, that reintroduces the ambiguity.
3. Delete unsigned_canonical_json, call zero_abi::canonical_json, promote zero-abi from dev-dependency to a real dependency of graphzero-pack.
4. Flip the two intentionally-inverted assertions in canonical_json_drift.rs (they are written to fail once the encoders converge, with messages saying so).
5. Record which manifests were hashed with the divergent encoder (deliverable 3 of the parent bead).
